children.text: Key Takeaways
Car accident injuries may worsen after the initial crash as symptoms develop over time.
Common injuries include orthopedic, skeletal, soft tissue, neurological, and internal injuries.
Whiplash is a common soft tissue injury that may cause delayed symptoms.
Internal injuries may not appear immediately and can require prompt medical evaluation.
Early medical treatment and documentation can help track injury progression and recovery.

Car accidents in Colorado rarely end when traffic clears, with pain often developing days later as mobility fades and everyday responsibilities start slipping out of reach. Many injured drivers and passengers search for answers once medical visits increase and missed work creates financial pressure, especially when symptoms refuse to fade.
Understanding common car accident injuries helps people recognize warning signs early, seek appropriate care, and protect themselves as the toll of a collision grows heavier. Our
Denver personal injury attorneys
have extensive experience helping accident victims navigate the challenges that follow a crash, while our
Denver car accident lawyers
provide guidance through every stage of the recovery and claims process.
Car Accident Injuries Statistics and Facts in Colorado

Car accident injuries in Colorado frequently result from high-impact collisions shaped by geography, weather, and driver behavior. High-speed highways, steep mountain terrain, and sudden weather shifts increase both crash frequency and injury severity, particularly when drivers underestimate road conditions.
Impaired driving continues to play a major role in serious crashes across the state. According to the
Colorado Department of Transportation

, preliminary data shows that 234 people died in crashes involving an impaired driver in Colorado last year, reinforcing that alcohol and drug impairment remains a leading contributing factor in traffic deaths despite ongoing enforcement efforts.
Colorado’s terrain and climate often magnify injury severity

. Mountain roads, high speeds, and sudden weather changes reduce reaction time and increase impact force, which explains why injuries in these crashes frequently involve the spine, head, and internal organs.

These statistics reflect what trauma centers across Colorado see daily. Many injuries worsen after the adrenaline fades, particularly spinal, neurological, and internal damage that does not present immediate symptoms. Early medical evaluation and informed guidance often shape long-term outcomes.
Common Types of Car Accident Injuries

Car accidents often cause layered injuries rather than a single condition. Even crashes that seem manageable at first can trigger trauma affecting mobility, cognition, and long-term health. Medical providers frequently diagnose additional injuries during follow-up visits as swelling increases and symptoms evolve.
Orthopedic Car Crash Injuries

Orthopedic injuries affect joints, muscles, and the spine, often limiting movement long after vehicles leave the roadway. Back injuries, shoulder damage, and spinal disc trauma develop when the body absorbs sudden force. Herniated discs and spinal cord injuries may cause chronic pain, numbness, or weakness that interferes with standing, lifting, or prolonged sitting. These injuries often require extended treatment, and insurers frequently question the severity when symptoms progress over time.
Skeletal Injuries: Broken Bones From Car Accidents

Broken bones remain among the most disruptive outcomes of a collision. Arms, legs, ribs, and collarbones commonly fracture when occupants strike interior surfaces or experience restraint forces. Even fractures that heal properly can reduce strength and flexibility, limiting job performance and daily activity. Skeletal trauma often occurs alongside
common car accident injuries
such as soft tissue damage, extending recovery timelines, and increasing medical costs.
Soft Tissue Injuries
Soft tissue injuries affect muscles, ligaments, and tendons and often receive less attention than fractures, despite causing lasting pain.
Whiplash remains one of the most common injuries
, particularly after rear-end collisions, when sudden acceleration or deceleration forces the neck to move beyond its normal range.
As outlined by
Johns Hopkins Medicine

, most whiplash injuries result from collisions involving abrupt changes in speed, with rear-end crashes being a frequent cause of this type of neck trauma. Symptoms such as stiffness, headaches, and reduced range of motion often intensify days after the crash.

Because soft tissue injuries do not always appear on imaging studies, insurance companies frequently question their severity, making consistent medical documentation and follow-up care especially important when these injuries interfere with work, sleep, and daily activities.
Neurological Injuries

Neurological injuries affect the brain, nerves, and spinal cord, often altering how a person thinks, feels, or moves. Concussions can disrupt memory, concentration, and emotional balance without obvious external signs. More severe traumatic brain injuries may interfere with speech, balance, or coordination. These injuries frequently overlap with
common car accident injuries
involving the spine, and insurers often dispute their impact because cognitive symptoms fluctuate.
Internal Injuries

Internal injuries present a serious risk because symptoms do not always appear immediately. Organ damage, internal bleeding, and punctured lungs require prompt diagnosis, particularly after high-speed crashes or rollovers. Abdominal pain, dizziness, or breathing difficulty may signal internal trauma that worsens without early treatment.
Common Causes of Car Accidents
Most Colorado crashes share consistent underlying causes, often intensified by environmental conditions.
Distracted driving remains a leading factor
, commonly involving cell phone use, navigation adjustments, or in-vehicle technology. Speeding also plays a major role, contributing to roughly one in five crashes statewide.
Other contributing factors include:
Impaired driving involving alcohol or drugs
Winter weather, such as snow, ice, and sudden storms
Aggressive driving behavior, including tailgating and unsafe passing
Failure to yield during turns or at intersections
Driver fatigue on long, high-altitude routes like I-70

Intersection accidents also occur frequently in urban areas like Denver, often due to failure to yield at turns or to ignore traffic signals, especially in congested traffic corridors where rear-end collisions are common. These conditions combine to produce many of the
common car accident injuries
treated across Colorado.
Things to Do If You Are Injured in a Car Accident

Steps taken after a car accident often influence recovery and legal outcomes, so medical care should always come first, even when pain seems manageable. Following treatment plans and attending follow-up appointments helps track how injuries evolve. Protecting yourself also means acting with intention early:
Seek medical evaluation promptly and report all symptoms
Keep records of diagnoses, treatment recommendations, and limitations
Document missed work, ongoing pain, and daily disruptions
Avoid detailed conversations with insurance adjusters before understanding your rights
These actions help preserve clarity around the full impact of your injuries, especially as symptoms evolve over time.
